title: Youth Engagement Summit (YES)
organization: Habitat Derneği, in partnership with UNICEF Türkiye (per Habitat's own description; UNICEF partnership not independently verified on a unicef.org/unicef.org.tr page)
description: 4-day in-person trainer-training summit; selected applicants become volunteer trainer-educators who then deliver one of 5 curriculum tracks (AI, climate action/green skills, 21st-century skills, design thinking, social skills) in their own region afterward.
selectivity_evidence: Applied per-track, selected applicants attend; no published acceptance rate found. Not claiming a selectivity_tier above open_enrollment without one.
current_cycle_label: 2025 cycle only (21-24 August 2025) -- no 2026 edition found anywhere as of this research date (2026-08-22), one year and roughly 5 weeks after the 2025 dates.
verification_status: VERIFIED_HISTORICAL -- carried forward unchanged from the original turkey_batch3_2026-08-21.jsonl research (not re-verified by this session). The 15-24 age range explicitly including foreign nationals, 5 tracks, and 2025-08-07 deadline are direct quotes from Habitat Derneği's own blog posts.
notes: DO NOT SURFACE AS A CURRENTLY-APPLICABLE OPPORTUNITY: the only confirmed cycle already ran and closed over a year ago (deadline 2025-08-07), with no 2026 cycle announced. Drafted per the coordination session's explicit instruction to capture this record with an honest cycle_status rather than leave it un-drafted, so a future session starts from what's already known instead of re-researching from zero. GEOGRAPHIC SCOPE CAVEAT (carried in the record, not just reported): source text says the programme targets 'Türk ve yabancı uyruklu gençlere' (Turkish and foreign-national youth) aged 15-24, which suggests foreign nationals may be eligible, but it is genuinely unclear whether this means foreign nationals resident in Turkey specifically or applicants from abroad -- eligible_countries left as an empty list (not ['Turkey']) rather than asserting a scope the source does not clearly state; do not read the empty list as 'confirmed open worldwide.' cost=0 is as directly stated in the source record (not an inference, unlike the TEMA record's cost field).

title: Lise Afet Bilinçlendirme Eğitim Projesi (LABEP)
description: High-school disaster-preparedness education project (LABEP): theoretical and applied training in disaster preparedness, first aid, and civic/community safety, historically delivered through direct partnerships between AKUT Vakfı (or a regional AKUT team) and individual schools, ending in a multi-day closing camp. AKUT Vakfı is a foundation founded in 2011 by members of AKUT Arama Kurtarma Derneği (the search-and-rescue association) -- a related but legally distinct organisation; do not conflate the two.
selectivity_evidence: Not competitively selected; the evidenced instance operated through a direct school partnership rather than open individual application. Selectivity_tier not claimed.
current_cycle_label: Most recently evidenced cohort: 2025-2026 academic year, 20 weeks, TED Trabzon Koleji, per LOCAL NEWS (Taka Gazete) -- NOT per an AKUT Vakfı-published current page. The only AKUT Vakfı-hosted page describing LABEP in depth is dated to a 2013 workshop.
verification_status: NEEDS_REVIEW -- carried forward unchanged from the original turkey_batch3_2026-08-21.jsonl research (not re-verified by this session). Self-flagged by its own researcher: no current, self-service individual-application path could be found on AKUT Vakfı's own site; the 2025-2026 cohort evidence comes from local press (Taka Gazete, Kuzey Ekspres) describing one specific school partnership (TED Trabzon Koleji), not from an official AKUT Vakfı page stating how an unaffiliated student or school could apply, what it costs, or a general age range.
notes: DO NOT INSERT AS READY_TO_INSERT -- draft only, so the next person who touches this starts from what's already known rather than from zero. cost, minimum_age and maximum_age are left null because the source explicitly could not confirm them (grade_range='lise'/9-12 with an approximate 14-18 age correspondence is the ORIGINAL researcher's own inference from the grade band, not a number AKUT Vakfı states -- carried in this record's own fields as null rather than asserted as fact). Local press does describe LABEP as implemented 'Türkiye genelinde' (nationwide), suggesting real recurrence beyond the one evidenced cohort, but this record should not be read as confirming a general, currently-open application path for any Turkish high schooler.

title: TEGV Gönüllülüğü (TEGV Volunteering)
organization: Türkiye Eğitim Gönüllüleri Vakfı (TEGV / Educational Volunteers Foundation of Turkey)
description: Structured volunteering with four role types: Etkinlik Gönüllüsü (activity volunteer, remote or in person), Destek Gönüllüsü (support volunteer), Eğitmen Gönüllü (trainer volunteer), Kurumsal Gönüllülük (corporate volunteering). Seven-stage onboarding: foundation introduction, application form, information meeting, basic training, document upload, orientation, programme training.
application_open_date: Three fixed annual intakes: 1 September, 2 January, 1 June
selectivity_evidence: Not competitively selected; onboarding-gated rather than merit-selected. Selectivity_tier not claimed above open_enrollment.
current_cycle_label: Rolling with 3 fixed annual intake windows (Sep 1 / Jan 2 / Jun 1)
verification_status: VERIFIED_CURRENT -- carried forward from thincat_volunteering_2026-08-21.jsonl (not re-verified by this session). Age floor (15), under-18 in-person guardian registration, the 15-17 'istisnai gönüllülük' (exceptional volunteering) route, the three annual intake dates, and the volunteer role types are direct quotes from TEGV's own page.
notes: STRUCTURAL AVAILABILITY CAVEAT CARRIED IN THIS RECORD: the 15-17 route is explicitly described by TEGV itself as dependent on permission processes and quotas ('Kontenjanlar dolunca başvurular kapanabilir') -- availability for any specific 15-17-year-old applicant is genuinely uncertain and should be surfaced as such, not presented as guaranteed. One of very few Turkish volunteering routes that explicitly reaches under-18s. SOURCE-AUTHORITY: tegv.org fails looksOfficial() (plain .org, no .edu/.ac/.gov match).

title: European Solidarity Corps
description: The EU's flagship structured youth volunteering scheme. Three routes, verbatim from the official page: 'You can volunteer abroad, solo or in a team'; 'You can set up your own project in your community'; 'Humanitarian Aid Volunteering'. Registration via the European Solidarity Corps portal, then application to individual projects run by participating organisations.
application_requirements: registration on the European Solidarity Corps portal
selectivity_evidence: Not centrally selected; individual participating organisations select for their own projects. Selectivity_tier not claimed.
current_cycle_label: Rolling, project-by-project, no fixed application date
verification_status: VERIFIED_CURRENT -- carried forward from thincat_volunteering_2026-08-21.jsonl (not re-verified by this session). Age range (18-30, humanitarian aid to 35), the three volunteering routes, the grants-to-organisations funding model, and the portal-registration requirement are direct quotes from the official EU Youth Portal.
notes: AGE FLOOR IS THE HEADLINE FINDING, NOT A FOOTNOTE: minimum_age=18 (35 for the humanitarian-aid track only) means Europe's single largest, most obvious structured youth volunteering programme is structurally out of reach for essentially all of ORYN's 14-18 core users -- only actionable for a graduating senior. This is a real fact about the volunteering-for-teens space in Europe, not a gap in this lane's research: the flagship programme genuinely does not serve this age band. Recorded with minimum_age=18 stored strictly so the product does not surface it to a 15-year-old as something they can act on now. No participant cost or eligible-countries list stated on the official page (links to a 'Countries covered' page not enumerated in the fetched content) -- left null/empty rather than guessed. SOURCE-AUTHORITY: youth.europa.eu fails looksOfficial() (plain .eu, no .edu/.ac/.gov match) despite being an official European Commission programme.
